title: How to register notifications and critical alerts on the Irricontrol Platform?

blocks.text: The objective of this article is to teach the user how to register notifications and critical alerts on the Irricontrol Platform. To do this, the user should follow the procedure below:
1 - Access the platform’s main menu and look for the “Notifications” option.

2 - The following tab will be displayed for the user. To proceed, simply select the equipment for which the notification should be registered — among the options: pivot, pivot monitors, and pumps — and click the “Register Notifications” button.
3 - In the first tab, you must enter a name for the notification group.

4 - In tab number 2, you must define a time range for the notification group to operate, or leave the “All day” option selected as a reference. In the example below, we selected the time from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m.
5 - In tab number 3, you must select the devices that will be programmed to respond to those notification alerts.
6 - In tab number 4, you must select the reasons for which the devices should be notified, from the available options.

7 - Options such as misalignment, pressure failure, power outage, unknown error, and stop button pressed (while pump is on) also have the possibility of enabling a critical alert, providing an extra layer of safety for the user.

The Critical Alert feature overrides any restrictions imposed by the device being used — such as a mobile phone or tablet running the Irricontrol Platform app — for example, silent mode. This way, the user receives more intense notifications from the platform.
8 - Finally, simply select the "Finish" button to complete the registration of your notification.
9 - And confirm the registration by clicking the "Create" button.
10 - The registered notification will be displayed alongside the initial notification registration screen.
11 - If you need to register more notifications, simply click the “Register Notifications” button again.

12 - To edit, delete, or enable/disable a created notification, simply select the corresponding options within the notification box. The “Show Reasons” button displays the registered reasons for that notification, as previously described.

title: Getting to Know the Smart Farm

blocks.text: Welcome to the future of agriculture - the Smart Farm. Imagine a place where all Irricontrol products work in harmony, creating the perfect setting for communication and monitoring.
1. Mesh Network Concept

The operation of a Smart Farm is based on the concept of a Mesh Network, in which connected devices (nodes or information points) have the ability to communicate with each other. Within this network model, if a path between two nodes is interrupted, a reorganization occurs to establish a new path for communication.
In the case of Irricontrol’s Mesh Network, the equipment used for communication is the XBee radio, which is utilized in the Central, Irripump, Level Meter, SPOTi, and GPS Kit.
2. Components and Structures
2.1 Central

Usually located at the farm headquarters, we have the Central, always connected to the internet, receiving information from the products and initiating operations with a simple radio signal. The importance of the Central is to ensure data exchange between the radios in the Irricontrol network and the Irricontrol Platform. It is generally installed in an accessible and easy-to-maintain location to ensure good connectivity with the repeaters and other equipment in the network.
2.2 Bivolt Repeater

The repeater’s function is to extend the connectivity of the Irricontrol network to more distant locations. The bivolt repeater, also known as a plug-in repeater, is powered by the farm’s electrical network and is essential for some installations. Through the connection with the central unit, the signal propagated by it is then spread to the other equipment in the network by the repeaters installed on the farm.
The repeaters are installed at high points to ensure a quality line of sight with the other equipment.
2.3 Solar Repeater

Like the bivolt repeater, the solar-powered version has the same function. The advantage is that it does not require power from the farm’s electrical network, making it essential for some installations.
Like the central unit, the repeaters are also installed at high points to ensure a quality line of sight with the other equipment.
2.4 Control Panel

Responsible for the overall command of the pivots, Irricontrol panels ensure efficient and safe control of central pivots. The first example is the SmartConnect, a panel available for Bauer pivots, containing all of Irricontrol’s automation technology with both digital and analog functionality in a single panel, enabling fully remote control through the Irricontrol Platform

For the Nexus product, it is used to ensure efficient and safe remote control of central pivots with the help of the Irricontrol Platform. It can be installed on any brand and model of pivot, bringing more agility in the field.
Both types of panels constantly communicate with the GPS on the last tower, ensuring precise information about the pivot’s positioning.
2.5 GPS Kit
Comprising the Irrimesh and GPS, this kit is responsible for monitoring and bringing the pivot’s connectivity to the Irricontrol Platform.
The GPS KIT consists of: GPS + Irrimesh radio + pressure sensor (optional), so there are two types of GPS KIT: with pressure sensor and without pressure sensor.
The Irrimesh radio is usually installed at the center of the pivot, while the GPS is positioned on the last tower of the pivot.
The importance of a good connection between the GPS on the last tower and the controller ensures important information about the pivot’s position to be displayed on the Irricontrol Platform.
2.6 SPOTi

Considered a peripheral device, the SPOTi is responsible for remotely turning on the pivot pump. The purpose of this equipment is to replace the pump control cable when Irricontrol control panels with automation are already in place. In specific cases, this cable can be damaged by machinery, making replacement difficult as it is an underground cable.
The best solution is automation through SPOTi, avoiding any problems caused by cable damage.
2.7 Level Meter

Through a sensor, the product has the ability to measure the level of reservoirs, rivers, and wells. The goal is to control the water flow to be used from the reservoirs, ensuring there is no shortage during times of need.
2.8 Irripump

We use the Irripump to monitor the intake pumps, allowing remote commands. It works in conjunction with the level meter, providing insights on when to pump water again through the Irricontrol Platform.
2.9 and 2.10 Irricontrol Platform and User/Client

The data obtained from all sensing is stored in the cloud, so the client can access information and obtain accurate reports through the Irricontrol Platform. The platform’s goal is to ensure total control and monitoring of the equipment through a mobile app in a simple, easy, and intuitive way.

title: How do Pivot Reports work?

blocks.text: In Pivot Reports all pivot's operation data are presented. It shows the amount of hours worked in each time, total cost of the pivot in a specific period, the pivot's unexpected stops, voltages and pressures in the pivot, total amount of rainfall in a specific period, among other information.

To enable pivot reports, it is necessary to enable this option in the Edit Farm page, on the Pivot Reports tab. After that, for the reports to be correct, all pivot data must be entered correctly. In case of doubts on how to enable this option, take a look at the article "How to edit pivot's information?" to know more.
Specific Period

The established period is fundamental for showing the data in the time range in which you want to analyze the data. To configure it, just click on the icon at the top right of Operations Summary to edit it, as shown below.
Data Extraction
Click on the button   to extract all the pivot reports data in an Excel spreadsheet.
Charts
Wet Work Hours

This chart shows the amount of hours that the pivot worked wet during the periods previously configured in Edit Pivot (To know how to configure them, access the article "How to edit pivot's information?").
PH: Peak Hours
OPH: Off-Peak Hours
NT: Night Time
In addition, it is also possible to view the total amount of water used (m³) within the period specified in Total Volume.
By clicking on the three dashes at the top of the chart (highlighted below), it is possible to download it in the SVG, PNG or CSV formats.
Total Cost
The Total Cost chart shows all expenses presented over the established period. In it, it is possible to check the costs for each time range: PH (Peak Hours), OPH (Off-Peak Hours) and NT (Night Time).

To define the cost per KWh established by the Concessionaire responsible for supplying energy on the platform, just follow the steps presented in the article "How to define the energy tariffs on Irricontrol Platform?".
Precipitation Chart
In the precipitation chart, it is possible to view, during the specified period, how the pivot irrigated along the entire pivot's work range.
Moving the cursor over the points in the chart, it is possible to see the angle and the water blade applied during the specified period.
Unexpected Stops
In this item it is possible to view the errors presented by the evaluated pivot over the specified period. It shows low pressure, power fault, safety and power surge errors.
Pivot Voltages (V)
In the Pivot Voltages chart, it is possible to view how the power supplied by the hired Energy Concessionaire is. In case there are sudden voltage oscillations, it will be shown on the chart.
In the chart's bottom, it is possible to see the minimum, average and maximum voltages during the specified period.
In addition, at the chart's top it is possible to handle the functionalities in the chart. Access the item Charts Commands from this article to know more.
Pressure Comparative (bar)

In the Pressure Comparative chart, it is possible to view the pressure (in bar) in the pivot's last tower by angle during the entire work range when it has a pressure sensor. Beyond that, the chart compares the most recent data (last 1080 GPS answers within the period specified in the upper right corner of the chart) with the data older than the period specified at the three dots in the upper right corner (1080 GPS answers older than the specified period).
Clicking on the three dots at the top right corner, it is possible to change the date and time of comparison for the chart.
Rain Gauge
The Rain Gauge chart shows the amount of millimeters of rain in a specific date and the total amount of millimeters over the same period.
In this chart, it is possible to change the scale between Day, Week and Month. Also, it is possible to change the date range and the number of bars in which you want the data to appear.
By clicking on the three dashes at the chart's top right, it is possible to download the chart data in SVG, PNG or CSV formats, just as the Charts Commands topic of this article discusses.

Note: The Rain Gauge will only present the data when Nexus Panel or SmartConnect is powered up. However, the rain gauge will be counting all millimeters of rain during the period normally. When the Panel is powered up again, the data are presented referring to the days that it was turned off.
For example: If on the 24th day the Panel is turned off and on the 25th the power returns, the 25th day will show the rain data referring to both days 24 and 25, as shown below.
Charts Commands
In the top part of some charts it is possible to manage its functionalities. Here are the meanings and functions of each button.
With these buttons it is possible to zoom in and out on the chart.
With this button it is possible to select a specific area to analyze.
With the zoom activated, or with a selected area, it is possible to move along the chart area with this button activated.
With this button, the view returns to its initial settings.
With this button it is possible to download the chart's data in SVG, PNG and CSV.
Tables

By clicking on the Tables section at the top of the page, it is possible to have a summary of all operations over the selected period. For each command sent to the pivot, it is possible to know the initial date and time with the start angle, the end date and time of the pivot movement with the final angle, how long the pivot operated at peak hour, the total hours of operation and the water blade used.

You can still check all GPS answers (responsible for sending the last tower's position) by clicking on any spot of the Table. In this tab it is possible to view date and time of the received position, the pivot's angle, geographic coordinates showing where the pivot is, direction, precipitation, status, the pressure in the last tower and the counting of minutes in the hourmeter.

title: Knowing Irricontrol Platform

blocks.text: The Irricontrol Platform ensures complete control and monitoring of equipment in a simple, easy, and intuitive way. The video and description below present the entire left menu, explain the functionality of all buttons on the Farm’s Home Screen, and also explain the meaning of each pivot operation color.
1. Irricontrol Platform - Left Menu
The images below show where the left menu is located on the platform.
It consists of five items: Home, Profile, Farms, Devices, and Notifications:
Home:
Edit Profile: Through this option, you can edit and enter the user’s personal information.
Language: Through this option, you can select the language in which your platform will be displayed.
Log Out: When selecting the log out option, the user will be logged out of the platform.
Farms:
By clicking this option, you can search for your farm.
Devices:
In this option, you can see all the devices registered on the farm and also check the signal level presented by each of them.
In the “search radios” option, a scan is performed for the radios of the equipment belonging to the farm.
2. Farm Home Screen
The images below show how the farm home screen will appear.

The central symbol appears as indicated in the following image, turning blue when connected to the internet and gray when not. Without internet, it is not possible to send commands through the platform.
Regarding the pivots, in addition to their nomenclature, their angle and the date of the last update of that pivot on the platform also appear.
Notes: The angle appears only for pivots. In the case of pumps, for example, only the pressure measurement is displayed when there is a sensor.
3. Meaning of Pivot Operation Colors

items: Orange: The pivot is off;
Yellow: The pivot is stopped or energized;
Brown: The pivot is moving dry;
Light Blue: The pivot is irrigating;
Green:The pivot is scheduled to irrigate at a specific time;
Red: There was an error with the pivot causing an unexpected stop;
Dark Blue Stripe: Angle irrigated in the last 24 hours;
Gray: Possibly stopped.

blocks.text: 4. Meaning of Pivot Lines and Arrows

items: Dashed Line: Indicates where the irrigation will stop, i.e., the position of the pivot when the irrigation ends. This line only appears when the stop is scheduled in the irrigation command;
Solid Black Line: Indicates where the pivot towers are located;
Black Arrow: Indicates the direction in which the pivot is moving;
White Arrow: Indicates the 0° reference, i.e., the starting point;
Purple border: indicates the region that has been irrigated by the pivot in the last 24 hours.

blocks.text: 5. Other functionalities
To activate the full-screen view, simply click on the icon highlighted in the image below, located in the upper right region of the platform.
Through the bell icon, located in the left menu, you can receive and view alerts sent by the platform.
Additionally, you can register specific alert notifications for certain equipment.
To zoom in (+) or out (-), simply scroll the central mouse button or pinch to zoom on your mobile device.
Lastly, the highlighted edit pen below is used to view and modify the information of the farm in question.
In the bottom right corner of the platform, there is direct access to the Irricontrol support window.

title: How to change a user's permissions?

blocks.text: There are different types of user permissions that can be assigned. Among them, are: no permission, viewer, operator, configurator and administrator. Each of these permissions have different purposes on Irricontrol Platform, that way, they have limitations of functions in it.
No Permission
In this permission, the user won't have access to the selected equipment. In this way, the same will not appear at the Initial Farm Screen.
Viewer

In this permission, the user has access to the equipment and can view everything from reports to the sent commands. However, the user won't be able to send commands to the equipment, edit its settings and will not be able to access the Farm's editing page.
Operator

In this permission, the user has the same permissions as the Viewer, and beyond that, it is also possible to send commands to the equipment. However, the user won't be able to edit the equipment settings or access the Farm's editing page.
Configurator

In this permission, the user has the same permissions as the Operator, and beyond that, it is also possible to edit the equipment settings. However, the user won't be able to access the Farm's editing page.
Administrator

At last, as Administrator, the user will have all the permissions the Configurator has. It will be possible to access reports, command history, new sent commands, equipment information editions, Farm editions and, in addition, the user will be able to add and manage users.
How to access the user's Permissions
To access the user's permissions, access the Farm's editing page, clicking on the icon shown in the figure below.
After clicking on the icon, the page Edit Farm will appear. Click on the arrow in the right to view more options that include the Users option.
Clicking on Users, the window below will appear showing all users and administrators of the Farm. After that, click on the pen (  ) located next to the user whose permissions you want to change.
It will appear a new tab containing the user's name, his e-mail, the option to make him Administrator and all the Farm's equipment.

By Clicking on the down arrow to the right of the equipment's name, a list will appear with all available permissions. Select the one that better fits that equipment for the user, or change all equipment selecting the option beside All Equipments.

In case the user has to be an Administrator, just click on the Key next to the written Administrator. If it turns green, it means the user became an Administrator of the Farm. After editing the user's permissions, click on Save.
Note: Permissions are given per device, so it is necessary to configure the permission in all devices, otherwise the equipment won't appear to the user.

Power Ranges are periods of the day when there is a peak in demand for electricity. In this time range, the cost of electricity is higher. Thus, it is necessary to adjust it so that the reports are adjusted correctly.

There are three types of Power Ranges: Nighttime, Off-Peak and Peak. Nighttime are the hours when the lowest electricity tariff is paid. Check with your city's electricity distributor to see these schedules.

Editing the Pivot

In this tab, it is possible to view the radios used in the Central, the controller, the GPS, and the pump radio. Additionally, you can add some characteristics of the Pivot Technical Data Sheet. These characteristics are: flow rate, radius to the last tower, speed of the last tower, and irrigated area. Furthermore, it is possible to add the voltage settings, language, and name of the pivot. Location

The location is necessary so that the pivot can be located in the correct position and so that the equipment can work properly. Just enter the latitude and longitude of the pivot Center (Center) and the Last Tower (Start Reference).
Clock

Adjusting the controller's time is important so that the scheduled commands work properly. That way, leave it configured according to the current time, or change it manually. To do this, click on the down arrow in the right and choose the desired option to adjust it.
To adjust it, click on the down arrow in the right and choose between the two options existing. In the case of adjusting it manually, enter the time in the "Equipment Date" field.
Pressure

In this tab, it is possible to add the pump power of the pivot. In addition, you can add also power time, pump timeout, delay time, unstable pressure switch time, minimum sensor value, pressure sensor maximum range and sensor scale. It is necessary to select the kind of pressure reading according to the equipment installed on the pivot.
Definitions:

items: Pump Timeout: regarding the time limit for the pivot to pressurize, in case it exceeds this time, the pump is powered off for safety.
Delay Time: time after the pivot has just pressurized, there is a wait for the pressure to reach the last tower and turn on the pivot.

Unstable Pressure Switch Time: referring to the time after pressurizing the pivot, if there's any pressure oscillation below the minimum pressure, the pivot will still not turn off and the pump will try to return to normal pressure. If this time passes and the pressure is still below the minimum pressure, the pump and the pivot will turn off.
Fertigation pump: it is a system linked to the pivot that is part of the irrigation process. Additives that complement the irrigation of the crop can be added.

blocks.text: Rain Gauge
If the pivot has rain gauge, it is necessary to configure it according to the Farm's preferences. There are three modes: disabled, by value and by decrement.
Disabled: in this mode, the pivot won't stop due to the amount of rain, but the equipment will still measure the millimeters of rain;
By value: in this mode, the pivot will stop after reaching the established limit of millimeters of rain in the field "Value" on the right side.

By decrement: in this mode, the pivot increases the percentimeter (the closest to 100%) with the purpose of compensating for the amount of millimeters that rained. If in this last case, it has already rained the amount established in the field "Value", the pivot will stop irrigating and moving.
If the Rain Gauge is installed later, it is possible to enable it by clicking on "Enable Pluviometer".
Pause Time

Pause Time are time ranges in which the pivot shouldn't operate because the cost of electricity is higher. Enable Peak Time 1 and define the Initial peak time and its end. Finally, mark the days of the week that you wish to activate the pause time.
Additionally, it is possible to include the energy price ranges for three options: peak, off-peak, and reduced.
Segments

In some pivots, it is necessary to segment them in two or more parts. That way, Irricontrol provides this feature, where it is possible to create till five segments. To configure the pivot's segments, first insert the maximum angle that the pivot reaches. After that, define the start angle, the end angle and the segment name. Finally, click on  and add other segments to the pivot.

The example below shows how segments are configured. In it, Segment 1 starts at 0º and ends at 180º and Segment 2 starts at 180º and ends at 360º, totalizing the maximum angle that the pivot reaches, in this case, 360º.
If the operator wants to delete a segment and redo the operation, just click on .
Note: The Platform will not save the settings until all the segments complete the angle previously defined.
Endgun
In some of the pivots there's an endgun installed on the last tower and Irricontrol provides a tool to configure it. There are three modes for the endgun:  Always off, always on and By switch.

items: Always off: in this mode, the endgun is never on, only the pivot.
Always on: in this mode, the endgun will be always on while the pivot is moving.

By switch: in this mode, it is possible to keep the endgun on or off according to parts previously configured. Irricontrol Platform provides the possibility to create up to 10 segments in which the endgun will be on. To configure these parts, just enter the start angle, the end angle and click on . With all segments configured, the endgun will be activated at the established angles.

blocks.text: The following picture shows an example of an endgun turned on by switch. In it, the pivot will be on at the angles 0º to 125º, 160º to 323º and 336º to 360º. And it will be off at all angles that are not included in those ranges.
If the operator wants to delete a segment and redo the operation, just click on  .
Autoreversion

Some pivots don't complete the 360º turn, so it is necessary that as soon as the pivot reaches the end of the course, it returns and does not exceed the established limits. In this way, Irricontrol provides the feature Autoreversion, which has three modes: Disabled, By end of stroke and By angle.

items: Disabled: in this mode, autoreversion won't be necessary. It is used for pivots that complete the 360º course.

By end of stroke: in this mode, it is necessary to add a waiting time. This time is the time the pivot will stay in position until it starts moving in the opposite direction. The pivot will always make this reversion till it stops.
By angle: the pivot stops moving at an angle previously established. It must be added a waiting time. This time is the same one configured for the option By end of stroke.

title: How does radio project sizing work?

blocks.text: This article aims to provide the basic requirements for sizing an irrigation automation project by Irricontrol. Initially, the following requirements are necessary to size the project:

items: Stable internet connection: a single, specific point is required to establish the installation of the central unit;
Infrastructure: must be compatible with all the items offered for the composition of the structure to be used;
Signal study: used to identify the network mesh, direct line-of-sight points, and shadowing points

blocks.text: 1. Getting Started
To carry out the project, you should access the Cloudrf platform: cloudrf.com.
On the main page, to log in, you should go to the ‘my account’ tab.
1.1 My account
On the ‘my account’ page, after logging in, the following page will open.
To access the page where the network project sizing will be done, you should click on ‘web interface’.
1.2 Configuring the Signal Study
When the ‘web interface’ page opens, you should select the template according to the region (the criterion used is the frequency of the XBee radio, which varies according to the location).
To start the network study, you should use 2 fillable fields.
Site Tx e Mobile Rx.
"When the ‘web interface’ page opens, you should select the template according to the region (the criterion used is the frequency of the XBee radio, which varies according to the location)."
1.3 Tab - Site/Tx

In the mentioned ‘Site/Tx’ tab, the transmitter information is entered. The transmitter is considered the radio signal that seeks communication with other devices such as the central unit and repeaters. Three fields are required to be filled in this tab:

items: Latitude;
Longitude;
Height.

blocks.text: Latitude and longitude refer to the location of the radio signal transmission, for example, the location of the central unit, pivots, towers, and where the repeaters, poles, etc., were installed. The height is considered the height of the device that emits and propagates the signal.
1.4 Tab - Mobile/Rx
The ‘Mobile/Rx’ tab is where the receiver information is entered. The receiver is considered the device we want to communicate with. Only one field is required to be filled in this tab: Height.

You should provide the height of the installed device. By default, 3 meters is used, as it is the height of a pivot and consequently the device that mostly seeks connection, with exceptions in some cases.
1.5 Finalizing the Signal Study
After filling in the information, you should press only the green icon. The following message will appear. The warning is just for configuration purposes and can be ignored without any problem.
The final step is to download the KMZ file.
2. Project Understanding
The downloaded file is opened in Google Earth for visualization and where the signal study analysis will be conducted.
The measurement scale indicates the intensity of the propagated signal in that area, as follows:
-65: Excellent;
-75: Good;
-85: Fair;
-95: Poor (but acceptable);
-105: Very Poor (do not consider).
3. Addition of Repeaters

The signal study is flexible and relies on the perception of the person conducting it. Where there is coloration, there is a network mesh where device communication is possible. In areas without radio connection, known as shadowing areas, solar/bivolt signal repeaters are used, as shown in the image, to propagate the signal.

The height of the Tx in these cases is considered to be around 5 meters, as it includes the height of the pivot plus the height of the tube where the solar repeater is installed. If the repeater is in another location, its height is also considered.
Finally, the signal study concludes with the entire coverage area having the equipment inserted into the Mesh network where they are located.
It is important to mention that contact with the client is vital to ensure that expectations are aligned.

title: What is the Irrifast?

blocks.text: 1. Concept
To increase productivity, Irrifast is the Bauer/Irricontrol solution that allows for higher speed operations in irrigation automation. Among the benefits of the equipment, we can mention:

items: Increases the efficiency and longevity of field equipment;
Provides higher operating speed and smooth motor starts/stops;
Reduces motor maintenance;
Delivers low application rates (mm) for quick irrigations and is suitable for fertigation;
Optimizes pivot irrigation systems for faster operation and detailed equipment information at each tower (future solution).

2.2 Last tower Model

For the Standard model, they are installed on each of the drive towers. This model uses microswitches to detect the angle between the pivot segments, aiming to control the rotation of the gear motors. The operating frequency of the motors is continuously adjusted according to the needs.
Regarding the last tower model, a distinguishing feature of this model is that it is connected to more solutions, such as GPS, position light, end gun, etc.
3. Operation of Irrifast

Each box has a frequency inverter to control the speed of the operation, considering that the last tower moves at a faster speed compared to the others, decreasing as each tower approaches the center of the pivot.
The last tower starts at 90Hz, and the others are modulated to ensure continuous alignment. To guarantee this operation, all frequency inverters must be parameterized.

items: It is equipment available only for Bauer pivots;
Operates with a working voltage between 340 VAC to 510 VAC;
Maximum speed of 400 m/h;
All towers must have Irrifast;
Does not operate with a hybrid model (conventional + Irrifast). It is suggested to use only one technology to avoid misalignment as shown in the figure below.

blocks.text: 6. Frequently Asked Questions
Does it work for single-phase pivots?

Even in situations where the power grid is not three-phase, the system can be used in single-phase 220 VAC power supply situations. However, it is always important to consult the dealer or Bauer to evaluate the system’s usage conditions.
Which gear motor model is recommended for this solution? Is it the same model on all towers?
The 1.5 UMC and 2.5 UMC models are recommended, with the latter being more suitable for uneven terrain situations.
Does it work on all pivots or only Bauer pivots?

The system works on both new and existing Bauer pivots. Customers with already installed pivots should be advised that, when this solution is recommended, there is a possibility that the gear motor assembly may be nearing the end of its useful life or have issues that could be exacerbated by using Irrifast.

title: What is the Anti-Theft System (SAF)?

blocks.text: In the field, security is an extremely important factor for the producer regarding cultivation preparation equipment. Since these are high-cost equipment, quality protection is essential to ensure the continuity of crop production against offenders.
1. Overview
Regarding general product specifications:

items: Designed to protect pivots and pumping stations against theft;
Powered by a battery/solar panel and installed on the equipment to be protected;
Uses a satellite system to provide protection;

Triggers an audible alarm and sends satellite messages when a signal disruption process is detected. The monitoring center uses this data, and a qualified team contacts the customer for clarification.

blocks.text: 2. Product Variation
For the SAF specifically, there are four product variations:

items: Variations by type of equipment protected: pivot or pump house;
In the pivot, it protects the entire electrical part of the central panel, collector ring, aerial cable, intermediate boxes, motor reducer cable, and the motor reducer itself;
In the pump house, it protects the transformer, cables from the transformer to the motor, pump motor panel, and the motor;
Voltage variations: 110V or 220V.

blocks.text: 3. Practical Installation

The product comes with an installation support to be attached to the protected equipment, electrical connectors, and cables for installations.
The installation time is on average 2 hours for other brands of pivots and 30 minutes for Bauer pivots.
It has a remote control to activate and deactivate the alarm system and control the satellite signal.

items: Some RTK systems may be affected by the satellite signal; based on this, the SAF provides an option to turn off this signal.

blocks.text: 4. Reliability Guarantee

To ensure product reliability, the SAF sends a specific notification to the customer if the battery loses charge.
Another extremely valuable aspect is the time taken between the alarm being triggered and the satellite message being received, which is between five seconds to one minute.
Last but not least, the product integrates with the Irricontrol platform in a roadmap format.

title: What is Radio and 4G technology?

blocks.text: For this article, the content to be addressed refers to the connectivity necessary for the operation of Irricontrol’s Smart Farm. In this case, two types of connectivity are offered: Radio and 4G.

The choice of technology varies depending on the region and the type of connection it offers. For example, in Brazilian states, there is a lack of cellular network signal on farms. Therefore, the use of radio technology is recommended.
1. Operation via Radio

items: The radio connection is made through the XBee radio, forming a Mesh network on the property;
A Mesh network is a network in which all connected devices, or “nodes,” have the ability to communicate with each other;
Further addressing the concept, in a Mesh network, if a path between two nodes is interrupted, the nodes can reorganize and establish a new path to maintain communication;
The XBee radio can connect to: Central, Nexus, SmartConnect, Irripump, level meter, Spoti, GPS Kit.

blocks.text: 2. Operation via 4G

items: 4G connection, also known as LTE, is widely used in areas with a stable LTE network;
The equipment required for 4G connection includes a 4G gateway and an encoder. This set of equipment replaces the need for a GPS;
Currently, the compatibility of this system is limited to pivot automation.

blocks.text: 3. Basic 4G Architecture

The figure below represents the components of an LTE network (Core and Access). The eNodeB (Enhanced NodeB), considered base radio stations, perform tasks of processing, traffic control on the air interface, thus ensuring QoS (Quality of Service). It is also responsible for mobile handover decisions through communication between elements using the X2 interface.

The gateway between the access network and the core is divided between the Serving Gateway (Serving-GW) and the Mobility Management Entity (MME). The MME is responsible for user mobility and signaling, including authentication, connection establishment, and handover support. The Serving Gateway is responsible for forwarding IP packets between the mobile user and the internet.
4. Responsibilities for Using 4G Technology
Is a SIM card needed?
Who provides the SIM card? For the 4G connection, a SIM card is necessary. However, the responsibility of providing the SIM card and contracting the data plan lies with the customer.
What type of SIM card is needed?
It is recommended to use any micro SIM compatible with 4G/LTE. Additionally, we suggest acquiring the SIM card with a data plan already contracted to facilitate the process.
How much data does the equipment consume?

Considering the maximum use of a pivot, our recommendation is to contract a 1GB data plan per month. Furthermore, we request that it be a postpaid plan instead of a prepaid one to avoid possible interruptions due to forgetting to recharge.
5. Frequently Asked Questions
Does it work in areas with 2G coverage? Does it work in areas with 5G coverage?

The 4G connection is compatible with areas that have 2G coverage. 4G equipment will continue to support 4G LTE technologies, 3G such as UMTS/HSPA/HSPA+ and CDMA2000, and 2G technologies such as GSM and IS-95. However, it is strongly required that 4G devices be in areas with stable 4G network coverage.

However, the technology used in 4G equipment is not compatible with the 5G network. The 5G network uses a wave-based frequency that is the fastest in the wireless mobile communication industry. 4G equipment is built to receive frequency only from 4G or older network versions. Therefore, 4G equipment will not work on a 5G network.
On the other hand, 5G equipment will work on a 4G network. This is because 5G, instead of replacing 4G, only expands its capabilities.
Can I have a farm with both 4G and radio?

Yes, it is absolutely feasible to implement both 4G and radio connections on a farm simultaneously. Each of these systems operates on different frequency bands, which, in theory, avoids mutual interference.
4G equipment has the advantage of operating autonomously, without the need for a central unit. This makes them flexible and easy to install anywhere with 4G coverage.

On the other hand, radio equipment requires a more complex network structure to function correctly. Despite this, they are extremely reliable and can offer a robust solution for communications in rural areas.
Therefore, the choice between 4G and radio will depend on the specific needs of the farm, the available infrastructure, and the budget.
Is it cheaper to automate pivots with 4G?
In general, the cost difference to automate pivots with 4G is not significant and can vary depending on the commercial strategy of each region.
What type of connectivity should we use?
Radio:

Radio communications can cover long distances, especially with the use of repeaters. This can be useful in rural areas where network infrastructure is limited.
Radio communications are less susceptible to interruptions caused by adverse weather conditions or power failures.
Data speeds: Radio communications generally have lower data speeds compared to 4G networks, but for our operation, this becomes indifferent.
4G:

4G coverage can be limited in rural areas, depending on the proximity of cell towers.
The 4G network is generally reliable but can be affected by adverse weather conditions or network congestion.
The costs of using the 4G network may be lower initially, but there are ongoing costs associated with data usage.
The 4G network offers significantly higher data speeds compared to radio communications, allowing the transmission of large amounts of data.

title: What are central units and repeaters?

blocks.text: At first, it is extremely important to understand how a Smart Farm operates through the concept of a Mesh Network, in which connected devices (nodes or information points) have the ability to communicate with each other. Within this network model, if a path between two nodes is interrupted, a reorganization occurs to establish a new path for communication.
In the case of the Irricontrol Mesh Network, the equipment used for communication is the XBee radio, used in the Central, Irripump, Level Meter, Spoti, and GPS Kit.
1. Central

It is a device always connected to the internet, receiving information from the products and initiating operations with a simple radio signal. The importance of the Central is to ensure data exchange between the radios of the Irricontrol network and the Irricontrol Platform. It is usually installed in a low and easily maintainable point to ensure good connectivity with the repeaters and other equipment in the network.
1.1 Support
When planning a project, it is crucial to consider product variations based on the available infrastructure. The initial question to ask is: What will be the installation location?
Answering the question, there are three installation options, with specific articles for each type.

items: In a tower: "How does Tower's Support work"

blocks.text: 1.2 Cabling

It is worth mentioning that the cabling is analyzed according to each project and its specifications and operational needs. However, it is recommended that the power cable be shielded for greater durability and not exceed 10 meters in length.
1.3 Network Requirements
Does it require a minimum connection? A stable internet connection with a minimum data package of 30MB is recommended to ensure good system performance.

Does it work without an ethernet cable connection? Via Wi-Fi? No, our central unit requires an internet connection via cable, which must be directly connected to a router where the main internet connection is installed. It is worth noting that this will be the only internet point needed on the entire farm, as communication between the equipment is carried out via radio.
Note: For more information related to the central unit’s connection, please refer to the article. "Central without internet connection?"
2. Repeaters
2.1 Bivolt Repeater

The repeater’s function is to extend the connectivity of the Irricontrol network to more distant locations. The bivolt repeater, also known as a plug-in repeater, is powered by the farm’s electrical network and is essential for some installations. Through the connection with the central unit, the signal propagated by it is then spread to the other equipment in the network by the repeaters on the farm.
Like the central unit, the repeaters are also installed in high points to ensure a direct line of sight with the other equipment.
Compared to the central unit, the repeaters can be installed in two ways:

items: In a tower: "How does Tower's Support work"
In the center of the pivot: "How does Pivot's Support work"

blocks.text: 2.2 Solar Repeater

Like the bivolt repeater, the solar-powered version has the same function. The advantage lies in the fact that it does not require power from the farm’s electrical network, making it essential for some installations.
2.3 Solar Panel Notes
Solar panels require simple and periodic maintenance to ensure good performance and long durability. Here are some care and maintenance tips:
Cleaning:

items: Solar panels should be cleaned, on average, twice a year. Cleaning can be done with deionized or distilled water to avoid stains caused by rain. Avoid cleaning the panels under strong sunlight to prevent quick drying and stain formation;

Preventive maintenance: Includes semi-annual cleaning and a complete inspection of all electrical components (modules, inverter, string box, and connectors) and mechanical components (supports and mounting structure) to optimize performance, identify/repair damage, and prolong the equipment’s lifespan;
Attention to external factors: Solar panels can be damaged by external factors such as nearby construction or heavy rains, like hail.

blocks.text: Regarding the battery:

Solar panels work in conjunction with a battery system. These are used to store the electrical energy generated by the photovoltaic solar panels during periods of higher solar radiation. This way, the energy can be used later at night or on cloudy days.
Battery duration on cloudy days:

Considering a scenario of reduced amperage consumption, the battery would be able to maintain the charge for four days. This is valid even in a situation where there is a total interruption of the solar panel responsible for charging the battery.
2.4 Project Sizing

It is important to mention that a complete project study is carried out regarding the installation of the above equipment with highly qualified professionals and specialized signal scanning software, as shown in the figure below.

Last but not least, it is strongly suggested, as an ideal rule for proper functioning, that whenever a central unit is sold, a repeater should be provided along with it. This ensures that the central units will always be installed in easily accessible locations, simplifying periodic maintenance. The responsibility of being in elevated locations falls to the solar repeater, which requires sporadic maintenance and does not have an electrical connection.

blocks.text: Endgun
In some pivots, there is an endgun and Irricontrol provides tools to configure the same. It is possible to set it up by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller.
In Controllers G2, there are three endgun modes: On, Off and by Angles.

items: On: In this mode, the endgun will always be activated while the pivot is moving;
Off: In this mode, the endgun is never activated, only the pivot;

Turned on by angles: In this mode, it is possible to keep the endgun on or off according to ranges pre-configured. In Controller G2, you can create till 10 segments in which the endgun will be activated. To configure the segments, just enter their start and end angles.

Sector

The Sector corresponds to the maximum angle reached by the pivot, so if the pivot can rotate one complete turn, its sector is measured from 0º to 360º. It is possible to set it up by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller.
The video below shows the steps to configure the Sector in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Segments

In some pivots, it is necessary to segment them in two or more parts. This configuration allows the division of the irrigated area into up to 10 segments, in a way that the irrigation can be scheduled in different ways for each one of them.

It is possible to create them by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. The video below shows the steps to configure the pivot's Sectors in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Pressure Configuration

In this item it is possible to configure parameters related to the pump and the pressure, such as pump timeout, delay time and unstable pressure switch time. Beyond that, for Controllers G2, there are three types of pressure measurement: On (pressure switch), Off and by Sensor. Some important definitions to configure this item are:

items: Pump Timeout: referring to the time limit for the pivot to pressurize, in case it exceeds this time, the pump is turned off for safety;
Delay Time: the following time in which the pivot has pressurized, in it there is a waiting time until the pressure reaches the last tower and the pivot turns on;

Unstable Pressure Switch Time: referring to the time after the pivot has been pressurized, in case there are any pressure oscillations under the minimum pressure, the pivot will not be turned off just yet and the pump will try to return to normal pressure. If this time is exceeded and the pressure is still below the minimum one, the pump and the pivot will be turned off.

blocks.text: These settings can be configured by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. The video below shows the steps to adjust the Pressure Configuration in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Clock

Through the Clock function it is possible to adjust the time in the Controller. Its configuration is necessary so that the pivots operate according to the local time zone and start and finish the irrigations in the scheduled hours. To configure the Clock in Controllers G2, just follow the steps described in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .

Pause time is a range of time in which the pivot shouldn't operate because the cost of electricity is higher. It is possible to configure it by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. The video below shows the steps to configure the Pause Time in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Power Delay

Power Delay is the time in minutes that the pivot must wait to turn back on after a power loss. It is possible to set it up by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. To configure this time in Controllers G2, just follow the steps described in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Autoreverse

Some pivots don't rotate a complete 360º round, so it is necessary that by the time the pivot reaches the end of the course, it returns and doesn't exceed the established limits. For that, there's the Autoreverse function, that will make the pivot change its direction automatically, changing the direction the pivot was before. To access this setting and configure it through Controller G2, just follow the steps presented in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .

To enter the pivot's GPS coordinates through Controller G2, just follow the steps presented in the video below. It is possible to insert them by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Radio

The Radio function available in Controllers G2 allows us to insert manually the radio numbers from GPS, Central and Pump. In addition, it is also possible to initiate the equipment configuration and test the signal level presented by them. It is possible to enter them by both the Controller and Irricontrol Platform. To enter these numbers in Controllers G2, just follow the steps presented in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Injection Pump

The Injection Pump is responsible for activating the pump used for introducing pesticides and fertilizers for foliar application into the irrigation water. It is possible to set it up by both the Controller and Irricontrol Platform. In the Controller, select option On, if you want the pivot to have the injection pump automatized together with it, or Off if the pivot does not. The video below shows the steps to configure the injection pump in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Voltage Limits

Voltage Limits configuration allows the costumer to establish a minimum and a maximum voltages in which the pivot is going to operate. If the supply voltage is below or above these limits, the pivot will stop automatically. It is possible to set them up by both the Controller and Irricontrol Platform. Some important definitions to configure this item are:

items: Maximum voltage: maximum voltage in which the pivot will operate, since if it exceeds this voltage the pivot will stop automatically;
Minimum voltage: minimum voltage in which the pivot will operate, since if the supply voltage is below the minimum the pivot will stop automatically;
Time limit: referring to the time in which the pivot can operate out of the selected voltage range, when this time passes, the pivot stops automatically.

blocks.text: The following video shows the steps to configure the Voltage Limits in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .

After installing an Irricontrol's Controller, it is necessary to enter the voltage, measured on the Transformer Input, in the Voltage Calibration settings. The voltage must be measured with the help of a multimeter in AC scale. To calibrate the voltage in Controllers G2, just follow the steps described in the video below. Through this setting it is possible to view information about the pivot's operation time, showing for how much time the pivot operated in wet mode, with the endgun on, the pump time and the injection pump time. All these data count since the moment the equipment was powered on for the first time. To access the Operation Time in Controllers G2, just follow the steps presented in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Rainmeter

When the pivot has a rainmeter, it must be configured according to the Farm's preferences. This configuration can be done by both Irricontrol Platform and the Controller. To do this, in the controller there are two stop condition modes: by value and by decrease.

items: By value: in this mode, the rainmeter keeps the same water blade of the pivot, which makes the pivot stop after reaching this established limit of millimeters of rain.
By decrease: in this mode, the pivot increases the percentimeter (closest to 100%) with the purpose to compensate the amount of millimeters that rained during irrigation.

blocks.text: Through Controller G2 it is also possible to view the daily and monthly rain measurement and make a test to know if the controller is communicating with the rain gauge. In addition, it is necessary to pay attention to the scale value, which in this case should be 2 mm.
The video below shows the steps to configure the Rainmeter in Controllers G2. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .

In Controllers G2, there is also the option to visualize the pivot's Operation Time in Time Ranges. In this item, it is possible to choose the time range in hours and days of week in which you wish to know the time the pivot operated, considering that the data will be counted since the moment the equipment was powered on for the first time. The video below shows how to configure these time ranges to view the pivot's operation time in them. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .

Error Log

During irrigation, it can happen some problems that end up stopping the pivot. That way, Irricontrol shows what these errors are on the controller's screen and also on the platform, so that the user is aware of its operation. The function that allows us to see these errors is the Error Log, that can be found in Controllers G2 just like described in the video below. This function is activated only when the controller is connected to pivots with HMI interface. It is used to configure the controller to work in pivots with HMI panel. To activate it, just follow the steps described in the video below. To enable english subtitles in the video, click on the icon .
Alignment

This option is used to do the alignment procedure. The alignment mode cancels the safety connection and moves the pivot without moving the last tower with the purpose to align the other towers. In this setting, you can choose options on or off, if option on is selected, it is necessary to choose the direction that the pivot will move in this mode, so forward or reverse. The video below shows how to do this procedure in Controllers G2.
Pressure Failure Configuration

This function determines how the controller should be configured to circumvent possible pressure failures. For this, when this function is enabled, three options must be configured: restart time, maximum number of attempts to restart the pump, and reset time between attempts.
About

The About function allows us to visualize information about the version of the controller in question. On it, you can see the versions of the hardware, the firmware and the version of the protocol used in the module's radio, as well as the controller's radio number. title: Whats is the portfolio of Irricontrol panels?

blocks.text: 1. SmartConnect

The SmartConnect is a robust panel used to ensure efficient and safe control of central pivots. It is an equipment available for Bauer pivots, containing all of Irricontrol’s automation technology, allowing for fully remote control through the Irricontrol platform.

The SmartConnect has two modes of operation: analog and digital. In analog mode, it focuses on operational safety to bypass any impediments in digital operation, ensuring the continuity of the equipment’s operation. The video below shows an overview of the SmartConnect panel.
1.1 Internal part of the SmartConnect panel
In the image above, the SmartConnect panel is divided into three levels, each with its own importance for the equipment’s operation.

items: At the upper level (1), there are components responsible for the control and protection of the power section;
At the intermediate level (2), there are components responsible for the control and logic of the pivot’s operation, or the command section;
At the lower level (3), there are components responsible for organizing the connections and power cabling of the pivot.

blocks.text: Note: For more information on the operation of the SmartConnect panel, please refer to the article. "How does Irricontrol s SmartConnect G2 Panel work?"
1.2 SmartConnect Differentials

items: Two modes of operation in the same equipment (analog and digital);
Internal protections against failures (electrical and electronic);
Ease of replacement of internal parts (WEG);
Low maintenance of Irricontrol electronic components.

blocks.text: 1.3 Operation in Analog Mode
To operate the SmartConnect panel in analog mode, there are three switches and a button at the bottom to start operations.

items: Switch 1: indicates the option for the pivot to operate in dry mode (moving without irrigating) and wet mode (moving while irrigating);
Switch 2: activation in digital mode (using the display) or analog mode (using the switches);
Switch 3: indicates the direction of pivot operation. Reverse (counterclockwise) and Forward (clockwise);
Power Button: before being activated, the percentage meter must be adjusted (shown in the next slide).

blocks.text: 2. Nexus

The Nexus equipment is used to ensure the effective and safe remote management of central pivots through the Irricontrol platform. It confirms that remote commands are correctly executed on the pivot, thus ensuring the planned operations are carried out.

Ideal for situations where you want to automate central pivots from different manufacturers and models, consolidating them into a single integrated platform. Pivots from brands such as Bauer, Valley, Lindsay, Carborundum, Krebs, Irrigabras, among others, can be controlled by Nexus. This allows farms with pivots from different brands to be integrated and managed on the same Irricontrol platform.
2.1 Nexus Variations
2.2 Nexus Differentials

items: Nexus, due to its smaller size and quick installation on any model and brand of pivot, has more practical and easier maintenance;
Modernizes the pivot with Irricontrol technology.

title: How does Irricontrol's SmartConnect G2 Panel work?

blocks.text: In the Panel's analog version, the controller is disabled and the use of the buttons on the box lid is enabled.

To turn on the pivot in analog mode for the first time, turn the digital/analog switch to analog position. Choose the operating mode (wet or dry) and the direction (forward or reverse). And finally, press the button "start".

In addition, here, there's also a way of turning the pivot on through the pressure switch. To do this, turn the digital/analog switch to analog position, choose the operating mode (wet or dry) and the direction (forward or reverse). After that, for the pivot to start moving all it takes is activating the pressure switch.
To facilitate the understanding of the operation, we have divided the Panel in 3 parts plus the electrical diagram. To enable english subtitles in the videos, click on the icon .
Part 1

These are the components located at the top of the panel, responsible for controlling and protecting the power part. As they work with high power, usually 480 VAC, it is necessary to be careful and make sure that the power is always off when handling them.
Part 2
These are the components located at the central part of the panel, responsible for the control and the logic of the pivot's functioning, which we call the command part.

In this part, it is located the device called "percentimeter", responsible for adjusting the time in which the pivot's last tower will be on and off within one minute. A percentimeter at 50%, for example, keeps the last tower turned on for 30 seconds and turned off for 30 seconds.
Part 3
These are the components located at the bottom of the panel. They are mostly responsible for the connections of the power cables and also the pivot.

title: Installation of Switch Contactor to GPS on the last tower

blocks.text: Objective
This article to explain and undersatand the process of installing a contactor on the last tower for the purpose of GPS installation.
Note: This type of installation is necessary for pivots that have the safety return being Neutral.
Development
For the installation, a contactor unit model CWCA0-22-00V15 is required, as shown in the figure below. This model is suggested for pivots 110V.

Note: For the 110V pivots, a 110V contactor is required. For 220V pivots, a 220V contactor is necessary. Another extremely important piece of information is that the contactor must have at leats one normally open contact and one normally closed contact.
Installation Location
Control box of the last tower
For the installation of the contactor, it must be specifically installed in the control box of the last tower as shown in the images below.
Electrical Installation
The contactor below is referenced in the following electrical schematic, as the connections should be made.
RC (Pivot Reverse Cable): Cable responsible for the reverse direction of the pivot;
FC (Pivot Forward Cable): Cable responsible for the forward direction of the pivot;
NC (Pivot Neutral Cable): Ceutral cable of the system;
P-GPS (GPS Phase): Phase of the GPS system;
N-GPS (GPS Neutral): Neutral of the GPS system;
A1 and A2: Contactor coil;
13 and 14: Normally open contact (NO);
21 and 22: Normally closed contact (NC).
Contacts:
13 and 14: These are the normally open (NO) contacts. When the coil is energized, these contacts close, allowing current to pass.
21 and 22: These are the normally closed (NC) contacts. When the coil is energized, these contacts open, interrupting the current flow.
Pivot Cable Connections:
RC (Pivot Reverse Cable): Connected to terminals A1 and 13 of the contactor;
FC (Pivot Forward Cable): Connected to terminal 21 of the contactor;
NC (Pivot Neutral Cable): Connected to terminal A2 of the contactor;

title: How to convert the Nexus 220V to 110V?

blocks.text:
Objective:
To guide the reader on the correct replacement of components that must be changed in the Nexus G2 220VAC panel so that it can operate at 127VAC when necessary.

Note:
All modifications must be carried out with the entire system de-energized.
Kit Composition for Conversion
Named "Kit to Change Nexus from 220V to 127V", this kit includes two contactors and one Surge Protection Device (SPD), all rated for operation at 127VAC.
Modifications to Be Performed
The required modifications must be carried out both on the Nexus panel and on the original panel of the specific pivot system.
For the Nexus panel, the originally installed contactor and Surge Protection Device (SPD), rated for 220VAC, must be replaced with models compatible with 127VAC.

As for the original pivot panel, a 127VAC contactor must be installed—or replaced, if already present—for pump activation. Optionally, a second 127VAC contactor may be installed to control the fertigation system.
Modifications on the Nexus G2 Panel
The comparison below, between the table and the image, shows which components must be replaced and their corresponding positions in the Nexus G2 panel.
Figure 1 – Items to be replaced inside the Nexus panel.
Instructions for the Modifications
Contactor
To replace the contactor in the Nexus panel, follow the steps below:
A. Inside the Nexus panel, disconnect the wires from the CWCA0-31 contactor (220 VAC);
B. Remove the CWCA0-31 contactor (220 VAC) and install the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
C. Connect wire 37 to terminal 1L1 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
D. Connect wire 2 to terminal 5L3 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
E. Connect wire 82 to terminal A1 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
F. Connect wire 29 to terminal 2T1 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
G. Connect wire 3 to terminal 6T3 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC);
H. Connect wire 83 to terminal A2 of the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC).
Surge Protection Device (SPD)
To replace the SPD in the Nexus panel, follow the steps below:
A. Inside the Nexus panel, disconnect the wires from the 275V SPD (220 VAC);
B. Remove the 275V SPD (220 VAC) and install the 175V SPD (127 VAC);
C. Connect wire 15 to the L/N terminal of the 175V SPD (127 VAC);
D. Connect wire 29 to the ground terminal of the 175V SPD (127 VAC).
Figure 2 – Nexus panel before replacement – with 220 VAC Contactor and SPD.
Figure 3 – Nexus panel after replacement – with 127 VAC Contactor and SPD.
Modifications to the Pivot Main Panel – Auxiliary Pump Contactor

To enable the voltage conversion of the Nexus panel, in addition to replacing the components within the Nexus panel, it is mandatory to install a contactor for pump activation in the pivot’s main panel.
To install the auxiliary pump contactor, follow the steps below:
A. Mount the CW07-10 contactor (127 VAC) in the pivot main panel;
B. Connect wire 15 from the Nexus panel harness to terminal A2 of the added contactor;
C. Connect wire 16 from the Nexus panel harness to terminal A1 of the added contactor;
D. Connect the phase and neutral wires from the main panel to terminals 13 and 1L1 of the added contactor, respectively;
E. Connect the two-wire pump cable to terminals 14 and 2T1 of the added contactor.
Figure 4 – Wiring of the pump contactor cables – 127 VAC.
Note: It is important to emphasize that the kit provided does not include the adaptation of the panel for the use of an injector pump intended for fertigation (pump control).

title: Central without internet connection?

blocks.text: Introduction

The Central is a plug-and-play device designed to work automatically when powered on and with an Ethernet connection. However, it may present some problems in its operation, which can be due to disconnected cables or even incorrect configurations. If the device is not connecting to the Internet, the user can try some simple procedures to get the equipment back to work.
Is the Wi-Fi "Irricontrol Central" or "SmartConnect Irricontrol" appearing on the cell phone?

Check, with the help of a cell phone, and near the Central, in the searches for existing Wi-Fi networks, if the Wi-Fi icon with the name Irricontrol Central or SmartConnect Irricontrol is appearing. According to what is presented in the figures below.
For Android devices
For iOS devices

items: If the icon is not appearing, check the power cables! Check the topic "Is power reaching the Central?".
If this icon is displayed, it can be concluded that it is not a problem with the Central's power. Check the topic "Is the Ethernet port working?".

blocks.text: Is the Ethernet port working?

To do this, he should disconnect the cable that leaves the router/switch for the Central. Then, he should connect a working test cable to the same port where the Central was connected and connect the other end to a computer. From there, he should access any web page to check if the port is working.

If the Ethernet port connected to the test cable is not working, remove it and connect it to a new available port. If it does not work, the Ethernet ports may be blocked for use. If it does work, the port where the Central was may be defective. So, remove the test cable and connect the Central's cable to the new available port, checking if the internet is working again.

items: If the Ethernet port is not released for use, check the topic "Is the Ethernet port released for connection?".
If the Ethernet port is fully operational, check the topic "Is the Ethernet cable working?".

blocks.text: Is the Ethernet cable working?

To check this, unscrew the Central's cover and disconnect the Ethernet cable, as represented in the figure below. Then connect it to a computer to check the internet signal by accessing any web page. This will verify if the signal is being delivered to the equipment.
RJ45 Cable to be disconnected for testing
If the internet does not work on the computer, the cable may have accidentally come loose during handling on equipment or even broken/damaged at some point.

items: If the Ethernet cable is fine, check the topic "Is the internet connection stable?".

If the internet works on the computer, return the Ethernet cable to the Central and remove its power for approximately 30 seconds. After that, plug in the power cable again and check the internet connection on the platform.

blocks.text: Is power getting to the Central?

Initially, check if the power cable is properly connected to a power source. If it is properly connected, then unscrew the Central's cover and check if LED 3V3 (D301), located near the battery (as shown in the figure below), is lit, meaning that the board is receiving power. If it is not lit, measure the voltage at the input and output of the equipment's power source using a multimeter.
3V3 LED Location (D301)
3V3 LED Location (D301)

Note: To measure the input voltage, the multimeter must be set to the AC scale (measuring 127V or 220V, depending on the power supply) and for the output voltage, the multimeter must be set to the DC scale.
Input voltage measurement

items: If LED 3V3 (D301) is not lit and there is no correct input voltage on the multimeter, then check the power cable;
If LED 3V3 (D301) is not lit and there is correct input voltage but not output voltage on the multimeter, the power source may be burned out. Contact the nearest Dealer with this information;
If LED 3V3 (D301) is not lit and there is correct input and output voltage on the multimeter, then the board may be burned out;
If LED 3V3 (D301) is lit and voltages are correct, contact the nearest Dealer.

blocks.text: Is the Ethernet port open for connection?

The central operates with an Ethernet cable similar to what occurs with a personal computer. In other words, if an Ethernet cable is connected to the central, it will connect to the internet like a computer. However, for network configuration, the port that the cable will exit the router/switch needs to be open for use.

Check with the farm's IT technician to see if the Ethernet port that the central is connected to is open. In other words, the farm needs to designate an IP to be used by the Central's MAC. Then, steps must be followed to complete the network configuration, for which you should contact the nearest Dealer.

items: If the connection doesn't work, contact the nearest Dealer.
If the Ethernet port is open for use, check the topic "Is the internet connection stable?".

blocks.text: Is the internet connection stable?
To do this, check with the internet provider if there has been any connection instability, temporarily causing a failure in communication with the central.

items: If the connection instability is due to the internet provider, wait for its return.
If the connection is stable, check with the nearest Dealer.

Note: After the proper measurements and checks have been made, screw the cover
back on, properly closing the equipment.

title: Is the pivot stopping by Voltage outside the allowed range?

blocks.text: In some occasions, pivots can present some errors that make the irrigation not to proceed. The Voltage outside the allowed range error is one of these. This message has the purpose to show and stop the pivot, when it receives an input voltage range far below or far above the voltages the equipment is prepared to work with.
The reasons for this error to happen are:

items: When the network voltage really fell and, in this case, it will be necessary to check the reason in the Farm;
There may be some phase of the pivot's three-phase that is not working;
Irricontrol voltage meter may not be calibrated;
Error with Irricontrol meter.

blocks.text: Although, if the voltage is correct there are some points to pay attention to for correcting the error. It can occur due to the lack of voltage calibration on the controller or, yet, due to some problem in the controller.
01. What is the first step?

Measure the Transformer's input voltage of the panel and check if it isn't too far from the pivot's Reference value found in the Controller. To do this, with the help of a multimeter and carefully, measure at the top part of the Transformer (Input), the points where the cables are connected.
Measurement on Nexus
Measurement on SmartConnect
After that, measure the voltage after the Transformer, the values obtained must be close to 110V. If there's no voltage leaving the Transformer, it is burned and must be replaced.
Measurement on Nexus
Measurement on SmartConnect
If the values are correct, follow Step 02 so that the pivot can move or follow Step 03 to correct the problem.
02. The step above was done but it is necessary to irrigate now, what can I do?
Irricontrol Platform provides an option for the producer not to be without irrigating in these cases, disabling the pivot's Voltage Control function.

1º To do this, access the Editing tab of the pivot in which the problem is happening (one must have a Configurator's permission in Users to do this, Click here to know more), by clicking on the green Pencil on the screen's top corner.
2º When you access the editing page, search in the GENERAL tab's lower part, the Voltage Control option. Click on the check (  ) to remove the selection and disable the option.
3º Notice that by removing the selection, options Minimum operating voltage, Maximum operating voltage and Timeout will be blocked for alteration.

4º After that, click on SAVE and wait until the Controller's Radio responds with two blue checks (  ). If you have any doubts about this, check the article "How to send a configuration to the controller through the Platform?".
5º When all the steps are finished, the pivot won't stop by the Voltage outside the allowed range error.
03. I want the pivot to show the voltage, what now?

1º To solve this problem, first you must confirm on the controller if the voltage is calibrated. To do this, check the article "How to calibrate the voltage in the Controller?" to know if your controller is already with the voltage's reference value.
2º If the voltage is already calibrated correctly, disconnect the green terminals at the controller's backside.
3º Remove the screws on the 04 plastic latches that hold the controller on the Panel with the help of a thin Philips screwdriver.
4º Open the controller's back cover, with the help of a thin Philips screwdriver, removing the screws on the controller's box edges, just like highlighted in the Figure below.
