blocks.text: 4.2. Does the SPOTi relay activate the pump contactor?

To know if the relay inside the SPOTi will activate the contactor, first, unscrew the IRRIPUMP cover, then send a command to turn on the pump. Observe if, when IRRIPUMP sends a signal to activate the pump, the relay positioned on the board will activate the pump contactor. In other words, check if the DK102 LED (Figure 5) positioned in front of the relay (Figure 6) will light up and if the contactor will activate. Observe if the contactor will activate by identifying the sound and by visualizing the switch moving from the O symbol to the I symbol.
Figure 5 - Location of the LED DK102.
Figure 6 - Location of the Relay that will activate the pump contactor.

items: If the relay does not activate the contactor, contact the Irricontrol Support Team.
If the DK102 LED lights up and the relay activates the contactor, check the topic "5.1. Is the SPOTI sending a signal to the pump?".

blocks.text: 5. Electrical Signal Verification
5.1. Is the SPOTi sending a signal to the pump?

The SPOTi is responsible for sending a signal to the pump to turn on when a command is sent. Therefore, send a command through the Irricontrol Platform and check the electrical signal that should be measured, with the help of a multimeter, at the end of the terminal that connects to the pump’s electrical panel.

items: If there is no voltage at the end of the terminal, contact the Irricontrol Support Team with this information.
If there is voltage at the end of the terminal, check the topic "6.1. Is the pump receiving power?".

blocks.text: 6. Pump Verification
6.1. Is the pump receiving power?
Check if power is being delivered to the pumping system.

items: If the pump is not turning on, check the power cables for damage or defects. Replace them if defective.
If the pump is receiving power and there is a Soft Starter, check the topic"6.2. Does the Soft Starter have any parameter errors?".
If the pump is receiving power and there is no Soft Starter, check the topic "6.3. Is the pvot electrical panel in order?".

blocks.text: 6.2. Does the Soft Starter have any parameter errors?
Check the pump’s Soft Starter system for any errors or issues that need to be resolved.

items: If there is a problem with the pump’s Soft Starter, refer to its manual to clear the memory and restart the pump.
If there is no problem with the pump’s Soft Starter system, check the topic "6.3. Is the pivot electrical panel in order?".

blocks.text: 6.3. Is the pivot electrical panel in order?

Check if any pump cables in the electrical panel are damaged or poorly connected. To verify the connection, gently pull all the cables; if any disconnect easily, reconnect them and tighten them properly.

items: If there are poorly connected cables in the electrical panel, reconnect all of them firmly.
If any cables are damaged, replace them with corresponding ones, following the equipment’s electrical diagram.
If you have any doubts about the cabling, contact the Irricontrol Support Team to check all the cables.
If the cables are in order, check the topic "6.4. Is the pump contactor activating?".

blocks.text: 6.4. Is the pump contactor activating?

The pump contactor should activate whenever a command is sent. To check if it is working properly, send a command to turn on the pump and observe if the contactor activates by identifying the sound and by seeing the switch move from the O symbol to the I symbol.

items: If the contactor does not activate and the cabling is in order with the electrical panel, replace the contactor.
If the contactor activates correctly, check the topic "6.5. Does the pump have mechanical problems?".

blocks.text: 6.5. Does the pump have mechanical problems?
Check the mechanical operation of the pump together with the farm’s responsible technician.

items: If there is a mechanical problem, repair it.
If the pump does not have mechanical problems, contact the Irricontrol Support Team.

blocks.text: Note: After the necessary measurements and checks, screw the cover back on, ensuring the equipment is properly closed.

title: How to perform tests on the Rain Gauge?

blocks.text: 1. Introduction

The Rain Gauge is used to control rainfall in a given location. This equipment becomes fundamental for agricultural irrigation. Thus, the rain gauge linked to the pivot reduces costs and proposes better soil management.
2. Rain Gauge Tests
The tests are essential for checking the correct functioning of the rain gauge. Therefore, there are three fundamental steps to be followed:

items: Stacks verification
Test on controller
Pulse test

blocks.text: 2.1. Stacks verification

Initially, with the panel turned off, unscrew the 4 Philips screws from the Rain Gauge box cover. Insert the batteries shipped with the Rain Gauge into the Battery Holder according to the correct orientation. From there, check if LED 1 on the board (located as shown in the Figure below) will blink and then stop, as shown in Video 01.
Video 01
2.2. Test on Controller
With the panel turned on again, follow the steps below on the controller:
Buttons Menu
2.2.1. Click on the Gear button;
2.2.2. Click twice on the Up Arrow button until the Rain Gauge icon appears;
2.2.3. Click on the Right Arrow button to confirm, so you will access the 1/3 tab of the Rain Gauge;

2.2.4. On the Rain Gauge tab, make sure the option is underlined in the On option. If not, click on the Check button for the first option, select the On option with the Left Arrow button and confirm with the Check button;

2.2.5. On the same tab, click on the Down Arrow and Check buttons for the Stop Condition. Make sure this option is set to Decrease. If not, find the Decrease option using the Up Arrow or Down Arrow button and click on the Check button;

2.2.6. On the Scale icon, change it to 0.2 mm. To do this, click on the Check button, then click on the Right Button, click on the Down Arrow button to change it to 0.2mm and click on the Check button;

2.2.7. Click on the Down Arrow button and access the 2/3 tab of the Rain Gauge. In this tab, check if all values are zeroed. If not, click on the Down Arrow button to access the 3/3 tab of the Rain Gauge. Click on the Down Arrow button, again, then click on the Check button and select the option to clear;

2.2.8. Access the 3/3 tab of the Rain Gauge using the Down Arrow button. On this tab, click on the Check button on the Start Test option and check if a ✔ appears. If an X appears, there is a problem with the connection between the rain gauge and the controller.

Note: The tests are essential for checking the correct functioning of the rain gauge and help to discover what is the problem when it is not working. However, in some cases, the problem is not in the equipment itself and may have been caused by external factors, such as insects and animals. Therefore, it is always important to check, especially in the water collector, if there's anything inside the container obstructing the passage of water, as shown in the video below.
Video 02
2.3. Pulse Test

For this test, pulses must be given to the rain gauge so that they are recorded in the controller. To do this, open the rain gauge housing according to Video 03 and then press the "Seesaw" with your finger until the end of the stroke and release quickly (exemplified in Video 04). Repeat this procedure five times to generate the value of 1.0mm Daily and 1.0mm Monthly.
Video 03
Video 04

If 1.0mm does not appear in the Rain Gauge tab under Measure, clean everything from the rain gauge on the controller as shown in step 2.2.7 and redo the procedure, ensuring the Seesaw is tightened. If it still does not show the correct measurement, contact the Irricontrol Support Team for more information.
After the end of this step and confirmation of the values, clean everything from the rain gauge in the controller, as shown in step 2.2.7.
3. LED's operation

To check LEDs, it is necessary to remove the Rain Gauge box cover by unscrewing the 4 Philips screws from the cover. From there, check the operation of the LEDs located on the board, according to the Figure below.

items: LED 1 - Check if when the panel is powered and the rain gauge is connected, this LED blinks periodically, indicating that the equipment is working correctly;
LED 2 - This LED flashes when a rain gauge reading occurs.
LED 3 - This LED flashes when there is communication with the Controller.

blocks.text: 4. How to reset the board

To perform this reset, click on the Reset button on the board next to the batteries and then release. LED 1 will flash, indicating that the board has been successfully reset. The Figure below shows the Reset button and LED 1 for checking. Video 05 shows how the action should proceed.
